title: VPC deployment guardian: orchestrated post-deploy API & model hotload checks
creator: Amala Reddy
description: Create an orchestrator for post-deploy validation of Private (VPC) deployments that runs API readiness probes, model hotload validation, light load tests, and smoke checks. The goal is to reduce manual validation time after terraform apply / helm upgrades and to catch failures where the control plane reports success but model serving paths are unhealthy (e.g. model fails to load, KV cache mis-wired, or runtime kernel mismatch). This ticket implements a reusable workflow (script + k8s Job + Terraform output hooks) that operators and CI can run after provisioning or rolling upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can be invoked with a single command or CI job that reads Terraform outputs and targets a single VPC deployment
API readiness checks return 200 for /health and a structured JSON for /v1/status within 10s
Model hotload validation confirms model artifact loaded into GPU memory and KV cache warmed for at least 2 representative prompts
Light load test executes 50 synthetic generation requests across 3 concurrent connections and reports p50/p95 latency and error rate < 1%
Smoke test includes structured output validation (function /tools calling) against a small prompt set; any regression marked and prevents automatic promotion
Output artifacts (logs, traces, prom metrics snapshot, and a summarized pass/fail report) are uploaded to the deployment run dashboard link
Failure modes map to clear remediation steps and produce a human-readable failure summary (model path mismatch, OOM, kernel error, permission denied to model blob, etc.)
implementation_tasks: Design CLI wrapper script: scripts/infra/vpc/guardian_run.sh (parse terraform outputs, authenticate, run checks)
Add Kubernetes Job manifest templates for model-hotload-check and api-smoke-checks under infra/vpc/k8s/checks
Create Terraform null_resource provisioner that triggers the guardian_run.sh when apply completes (opt-in flag: enable_postdeploy_checks)
Implement model hotload probe that queries /v1/models/<model>/status and validates GPU resident bytes and KV cache warmup metrics
Wire up lightweight load generator using vegeta/curl harness to simulate token-level requests and capture latencies
Add CI pipeline step (deploy-private -> guardian_run) in .github/workflows/private-deploy.yaml
Author a runbook for common failures and link to internal dashboard/alerting runbooks
Create a PR to update README and Console docs with the guardian flow and opt-in flag details
test_plan: Unit tests for guardian CLI argument parsing and Terraform output parsing
Integration test in staging VPC: run orchestrator against a canary deployment of a small model (quantized tiny model) and assert success
Chaos test: simulate model artifact missing to validate guardian reports 'artifact not found' and provides remediation link
Load regression test: capture baseline metrics and verify that p95 latency increase < 20% for minor config changes
End-to-end run in CI that triggers post-deploy checks after infra change and uploads artifacts to the deployment dashboard
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind Terraform var: enable_postdeploy_checks=false by default
Stage 1: Enable for internal staging clusters and for the infra team only
Stage 2: Enable opt-in for early enterprise customers via feature toggle
Stage 3: Flip default to true for all sandbox deployments once stable
Provide a mechanism to skip individual checks when necessary (e.g., skip-hotload for GPU maintenance)
Monitor errors for 2 weeks and revert if >5% of applies fail due to guardian timeouts
monitoring_and_alerting: Send guardian run summary to deployment-dashboard (Grafana panel) with pass/fail and key metrics
Create alert: guardian-failure-high if >3 consecutive guardian runs fail for a given cluster
Export prometheus snapshots for GPU memory, kernel errors, and model-load-duration during the run
Attach logs to S3 with a predictable prefix: s3://redwood-deploy-logs/<run-id>/guardian/*
Add a Slack notification to #infra-deployments with the summary and a link to the artifact bundle
notes: Trade-offs: running model hotload validation adds ~90s to post-deploy time for large models; we may expose a fast/slow profile to operators
Decision: start with non-destructive probes that only read /status and small inference calls to avoid corrupting KV state
Follow-up: evaluate adding a cold-start benchmark that measures first-token latency for full model cold loads
Design feedback from PM: include a human-friendly remediation card in the failure summary with next-step commands
Design feedback from Security: guardian artifacts must be stored with the same retention and access controls as other infra logs
